**Decision: the only lever with measured positive dose-response is training identity count, so the one mechanism is pooled-identity training (In-Shop and SOP products as one ArcFace proxy set and one full-fit bank, one encoder). Known method, not novel.**

**Why this layer, from the audited evidence**

- Every head/loss/init arm sits inside seed noise: centroid PCA −0.05/+0.19 pp, specific-impostor −0.02 pp, positive-tail +6 net hits, valid-anchor +0.08 pp, soup +0.05 pp, objective-conflict 1.25% opposed rows, head warm-up negligible. The readout is not binding, so a nonlinear or conditional projection is not warranted. Wide-256 fold and source-MAIN 1024 already showed extra head capacity does nothing.
- The fit-product scaling gate is the sole positive dose-response: halving fit products 2,004 to 1,002 cost 0.365 pp held R@1, interval [+0.15, +0.57], at matched 64k images. Fit R@1 is 99.36% versus held 95.5 to 97.7%, so the gap is unseen-identity generalization, which classically scales with class count.
- Not a closed arm: the SOP-prior falsifier and warm start were sequential initialization. Proxy synthesis made virtual classes from the same identities. Neither adds real identities concurrently.

**Ceiling, inference:** impostor scaling shows about 45 to 65 of 151 misses persist at one quarter of impostors, roughly 0.8 pp of the 6,354 queries, likely near-duplicate labels no encoder recovers. Two identity doublings at diminishing returns estimate +0.4 to +0.7 pp. That may still miss UNICOM 96.7 on In-Shop, and this smoke can only kill, not prove SOTA.

**Falsifier, TRAIN-only, CPU, existing cache, run in the repo venv (numpy is absent from system python).** Simulate cross-domain identities inside In-Shop using the path categories. A = one-piece and lower garments (Dresses, Skirts, Rompers, Pants, Shorts, Denim, Leggings, about 1,529 TRAIN products). B = tops and outerwear (about 2,520). Take only fit-half products from the pinned preflight split; evaluate only held-half A products, packed int8 self-excluded gallery.

```python
# frozen pretrained 1024-D pooler features, trainable Linear(1024,128), native objective
loss = arcface(head(x), proxies, y, m=0.3, s=64) + 8 * smooth_ap_bank_loss(...)
# control:   fit-A identities only
# treatment: fit-A + fit-B identities (about 2x identity count)
# sham:      fit-A + fit-B images, B labels collapsed to their 13 category names
# all arms: 1000 updates x 64, identity_balanced_batches, same seed, same held-A eval
```

Estimated wall: under 40 s per arm on 16 threads; if over 120 s total, cut all arms equally to 500 updates before reading quality.

| Rule, frozen before running | Threshold |
|---|---|
| GO: treatment minus control held-A packed R@1 | ≥ +0.3 pp, product-bootstrap 95% lower > 0 |
| GO also requires treatment minus sham | ≥ +0.2 pp (identity effect, not image effect) |
| Anything else | KILL the pooling lane |

Thresholds derive from the in-domain dose-response on TRAIN held data, never official.

**What GO changes in deployable code:** training only. Both trainers take a second dataset's rows with namespaced labels: proxies about 15.3k × 128, bank about 85k × 128 fp32 (44 MB), pooled identity-balanced schedule. Serving is untouched: same encoder, Linear128, 130 bytes, identical image-to-top-k latency. Compatibility test is the existing matched public-32 packed parity plus exact held-panel replay. Training cost estimate: coverage-matched budget is about 3.3× images, near 2,800 s per checkpoint at the measured 75 images/s.

**What KILL changes:** stop funding same-substrate head, loss, and init arms on In-Shop. The remaining routes are external identity data or a substrate change, both outside this cached-feature regime.
